title: L3 Mid-Review: Robust Mini System
story: You're building the startup sequence for a web server. Before accepting connections, it must read 4 config values, validate each one, transform them into the right types, and produce a final connection string — or a detailed report of everything that went wrong. This is what production code looks like: every possible failure is handled.
why: Combining Option, Result, ?, match, and if let into one cohesive function is the real-world pattern for initialization, configuration loading, and system startup.
analogy: This startup system is like a pilot's pre-flight checklist. Before takeoff, the pilot checks fuel (host), verifies flaps (port), checks weather radar (debug), and sets the callsign (name). Every item must be confirmed. If fuel is missing, checklist stops — no 'we'll figure it out in the air.' If weather radar is optional and broken, the pilot notes it but continues. Only when every required check passes does the control tower clear takeoff.
try_it: Remove the 'port' key from get_config and see the error. Add a 'max_connections' required config that must be 1-1000. Add a 'log_level' optional config with default 'info'. Use `if let Some("true") = get_config("debug")` to conditionally print a debug message. Add your own config key and make it required.
tips: Parse and validate in order: get the string, parse it, validate the number — each step depends on the previous
Use `match` on `string.str_to_int` result instead of `?` when you want a custom error message like 'Port must be a number'
Required configs use `?` to short-circuit; optional configs use `.unwrap_or()` to provide defaults — choose based on whether the app can run without it
common_mistakes: Mixing `?` on `Option` with `Result` return types — use `get_required` to bridge the two worlds
Validating port range before parsing — if the string is 'abc', you can't check if it's between 1 and 65535
Forgetting that `match` arms that return `Err` cause an early exit from the function — the rest of the code never runs
